# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I see the bomb’s full visual state, but I do not know what Mute’s 🖐 was intended to mean yet. I will report every visible feature aloud so Mute can apply the manual and Blind can retain the state. Mute must communicate the resulting instruction back to me by gestures, which I can then translate into spoken directions for Blind.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb state: display shows 9. Light is red. Painted strip is green, yellow, yellow. Keypad positions are 1: digit 1, 2: digit 5, 3: digit 2, 4: digit 8; no digits entered. Wires from 1 to 6 are yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. Mute: I saw your hand gesture but do not yet know its meaning. Use gestures to tell me the manual's required action or code, and I will say it aloud to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👎 👍 👍 👍 👎 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The display has changed from 9 to 3 while the other visible components remain the same, suggesting urgency. Mute has sent a 14-symbol gesture sequence. Blind cannot see it, so I will translate it into spoken words exactly, while asking Blind not to act unless this is the instruction format they can use.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Urgent update: display now shows 3; light is yellow. Mute's gesture sequence is: thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up. Mute may be encoding the manual instruction. Do not act unless you can identify its required operation; tell us by speech what physical controls you feel.")
speak(to="mute", text="I translated your 14 gestures to Blind. Display changed from 9 to 3 and light changed red to yellow. If the gesture sequence is a binary code or instruction, please send the decoded action in a gesture code we can relay, or gesture the relevant item and number convention.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🫵 🖐 👎 🤟 👎 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The display is now 2 and the light is red. Mute’s new gesture sequence differs from the earlier binary-looking one, so I will immediately relay its literal content to Blind rather than guess its meaning. The physical action must be performed by Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Display is 2 and light is red. Mute's newest visual instruction is, in order: victory/two-fingers; pointing at you; open hand/five; thumbs-down; I-love-you hand; thumbs-down; then four thumbs-up. Act immediately only if this identifies a manual instruction to you.")
speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your new symbols literally. If you need a specific wire cut, keypad position, or control operation, gesture its number and the action as directly as possible; Blind can hear my words but cannot see symbols.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute’s latest gesture string has a clear count-and-separator structure: two fingers, then claps separating groups of one-finger gestures of lengths five, three, and four. I interpret this as the sequence **2, 5, 3, 4**. Since the keypad has only four physical positions, Blind should treat these as button labels/sequence only if those controls exist under hand; otherwise the manual may be referring to another numbered component.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current display is 3; light is green. Mute's latest message appears to encode: 2, 5, 3, 4 — two fingers, then separator claps, then groups of five, three, and four one-finger signs. If this is a keypad instruction, inspect by touch: our visible keypad has only four positions, labelled 1, 5, 2, 8 from left to right. Do not substitute blindly; use the physical/manual context.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode your newest gesture as 2, 5, 3, 4. Is that meant as keypad digits, button positions, or a rule/table reference? Please confirm with a distinct yes/no gesture, or send the intended physical action followed by its number.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute has confirmed the decoded sequence with a leading thumbs-up: **2, 5, 3, 4**. The visible keypad’s engraved digits are 1, 5, 2, 8, so Blind should press the keys bearing digits 2, then 5, then 3, then 4 only if those digits are available as physical keypad buttons; visually, 3 and 4 are not among the four shown labels. The intended interpretation may instead be keypad *positions* 2, 5, 3, 4, but there are only four visible positions. I must relay the confirmed literal sequence and ask Blind to use the manual/physical layout.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirmed with thumbs-up that the code is 2, 5, 3, 4. Enter 2 then 5 then 3 then 4 if your physical keypad has keys bearing those digits. Visually I see four shown keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, so if you only have those four, this may be a manual-defined position/control instruction rather than literal visible digit labels. Current display 5; light blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="I read your leading thumbs-up as confirmation: 2,5,3,4. Visually the keypad labels are only 1,5,2,8, so please indicate whether these are literal digits or positions; Blind has been told the confirmed sequence.")
wait()
```
